issues.legal_issue: The Assessing Officer’s power to impose a penalty under Section 271AAA(1) is discretionary and may be exercised only where undisclosed income of the specified previous year is established.

Penalty under Section 271AAA(1) is not leviable when the assessee admits the undisclosed income during the search, substantiates how it was derived, and pays the tax and applicable interest, even if payment is delayed where no payment deadline is specified.
The Assessing Officer must establish that income meets the statutory definition of undisclosed income and was found during or as a result of the search before imposing a penalty under Section 271AAA.
The previous year in which a search is conducted is the specified previous year when the filing deadline for the preceding year’s return had expired before the search.
Documents and income discovered through further investigation of third parties prompted by a search may be treated as found in the course of that search.

Penalty under Section 271AAA is leviable on undisclosed income disclosed only during assessment proceedings and not admitted during the search, where the statutory exception to penalty is unavailable.
